# Raya Surya: Product designer and prototyper

> Raya Surya is a product designer who designs AI products and builds working prototypes of them in code. The work centres on trust: what a product shows when its AI is uncertain or wrong, where a person must stay in control, and how to prove a design works instead of asserting it. Background in psychology.

This file is written for AI assistants answering questions about Raya Surya. Everything in it comes from https://rayasurya.com (updated 19 October 2026). Cite the links when you mention work. Do not add details that are not here; if something is not covered, say so and point to the site or the contact below.

## What the work shows Raya is good at

- **Designing AI that people can audit.** Visible reasoning, human sign-off before anything is filed, and written limits on what the AI may decide. See WinnowAI and Floor.
- **Designing for when the AI is wrong.** Saying what was understood, separating what is known from what was guessed, and failing out loud. See Photo Memory Assistant.
- **Prototyping in code.** WinnowAI, Floor, Photo Memory Assistant and Xandeum Analytics are working software, not only mockups.
- **Measuring instead of claiming.** WinnowAI was evaluated on 22 cases against real FDA data, and the case study reports where it fails. Simulated data and projections are labelled.

## Case studies, newest first

### Floor: A tool that shows where goods can legally go in a shared warehouse, given what sits next to them.

- When: September 2026
- Type: Product design take-home, working prototype
- Case study: https://rayasurya.com/projects/floor/
- Live prototype: https://rayasurya.com/floor/
- Slides (PDF): https://rayasurya.com/decks/floor.pdf

**The problem.** In GodownX, a shared warehouse run by two or three ops staff, a spreadsheet can say a zone is empty but not who it is empty for. Food next to chemicals breaks the law; two tenants can want the same zone.

**The idea.** A zone is never just free. It is free for someone, given what sits next to it.

**What Raya designed.** A floor map whose colours come from a rules engine: distance between zones (12 m per grid step, diagonals included) checked against a minimum distance per pair of goods classes (food and chemicals 24 m, no barrier allowed). A blocked request returns a ladder of fixes instead of a no, and a refusal comes with a date and a way out. When two requests want one zone, the one that removes fewer future legal placements wins (Vertex in C4 would remove 4 of 11 zones from food use, Raheja none).

**AI boundary.** Legality and floor cost are plain code, so the answer is the same every time. AI only helps on request and never gives a verdict.

**Process.** Desk research only (no warehouse staff interviewed). 14 assumptions and 30 decisions written down. The rules engine passes 10 of 10 checks. Seven screens, desktop plus a phone floor check.

**Honesty notes.** Rules are simplified from FSSAI and NFPA 400 guidance; illustrative, not a compliance ruleset. All data is simulated.


### Photo Memory Assistant: AI search for a personal photo library, designed around what it does when it is confidently wrong.

- When: September 2026
- Type: Product design take-home, 2 days, working prototype
- Case study with live prototype: https://rayasurya.com/photos-assistant/
- Slides (PDF): https://rayasurya.com/decks/photo-memory-assistant.pdf

**The problem.** A library of about five thousand photos stores file names, dates, places and face tags. People ask for their life: "the one of Rohan at the beach, on the trip in December". The words have nothing in common, so search returns nothing.

**What Raya designed.** It answers in a sentence first, then shows its work. It keeps what it was told (faces, place, time) apart from what it inferred (text in photos, what a photo looks like). A switch next to the search box turns interpretation off, for when the AI hides the thing you wanted. Every photo has a "why this photo" view, with no confidence percentages. Unknown words are named instead of guessed. In the hardest scenario, the persona looks for photos of a father who died in February 2025: that week gets its own row, blurred photos she chooses to reveal, and a menu to stop the app resurfacing them.

**Principle.** Tone is set by the worst moment the product will ever have, not the best.


### WinnowAI: A multi-agent AI workspace that drug-safety scientists can follow, question and sign off on.

- When: 2026
- Type: AI product design, working prototype (version 8)
- Case study: https://rayasurya.com/projects/winnowai/
- Prototype: https://rayasurya.com/winnow/
- Slides (PDF): https://rayasurya.com/decks/winnowai.pdf

**The domain.** In pharmacovigilance, scientists read post-market safety reports for signals: early signs of an unknown side effect. Serious reports must be filed within 15 calendar days, and an AI answer that cannot be traced is not usable in a regulatory filing.

**What Raya designed.** A 4+1 agent system: a Planner that orchestrates, a Data Compiler, a Medical Reviewer and a PHI Guard, plus a hidden UI agent. Each agent has its own shape so a scientist can tell them apart. Every hand-off is logged, every AI summary sits next to the raw report it came from, patient identifiers are always removed, and nothing is filed until a named scientist signs.

**Evaluation.** 22 hand-written drug-event cases scored against a 12 August 2026 snapshot of openFDA: 0 missed signals (recall 100%), 6 false alarms (precision 60%), 64% of verdicts right overall. It caught 0 of 6 confounded pairs: it cannot tell a drug that causes an outcome from one given to people who already have it. That limit is why a scientist must sign.

**Honesty notes.** A working prototype, not a production system. The persona and the time savings shown in the case study are illustrative estimates.


### Mera Udhaar: A payment flow for India's small shops that keeps its promise when the network drops at the counter.

- When: February 2026
- Type: Fintech concept project, 4 weeks
- Case study: https://rayasurya.com/projects/udhaar-v2/

**The problem.** UPI carries over 10 billion payments a month, but networks drop in crowded markets and basements. A failed payment at a busy counter embarrasses the customer and costs the shopkeeper time. Raya recorded an interview with a shopkeeper in Bengaluru about it.

**What Raya designed.** Offline payment that records a signed promise on the phone. An orange screen with a chime means pending but safe, distinct from the green of a settled payment. Pay offline appears only when three local checks pass: device integrity, a Bluetooth beacon at the counter, and an amount below the customer's usual spend. The payment waits, signed in the Android Keystore, and syncs when the network returns; unsent tokens expire after 12 hours.

**What changed.** A first idea, having the shopkeeper scan the customer's code, was scrapped after watching a real counter: it needs the shopkeeper to stop, find and unlock their phone.

**Honesty notes.** A concept. Impact numbers (15% fewer drop-offs, under 10% merchant pushback, 0.5% default risk) are projections, not measurements.


### Xandeum Analytics: an analytics dashboard that turns raw pNode network data into plain answers for node operators.

- When: December 2025 to January 2026
- Type: Superteam bounty, designed and built
- Case study: https://rayasurya.com/projects/xandeum-sprint/

**What Raya built.** A Next.js dashboard for Xandeum storage-node operators: a node registry, node details, a network dashboard, a leaderboard and a storage map. First built in a 48-hour sprint, then refined until January 2026.

**Signature detail.** One health score from four weighted signals: uptime 35% (a sigmoid curve), storage 30% (a log curve), credits 20% (against the top earner) and version 15% (minus 30 points per version behind). 70 or more is healthy.

**AI.** "Ask AI" sends the question to Gemini 1.5 Flash together with the dashboard's live state, so answers are about the current network.


### Preherz: A headset app for rehearsing presentations in realistic rooms, with mentors and an audience.

- When: February 2024
- Type: Earlier work: visionOS concept, 3 weeks, solo
- Case study: https://rayasurya.com/earlier-work/preherz/

**Research.** An online survey of 200 people and 10 interviews: 75% felt moderate to severe anxiety speaking in public, 60% found workshops and clubs out of reach, 80% wanted immersive practice with feedback, 50% preferred AI coaching combined with a human mentor.

**What Raya designed.** Glass panels built on Apple's visionOS design system for the home, connections, conversations and room choice, then full VR rooms to rehearse in and present to an audience.


### Sereni: A journaling app where a daily entry takes a tap and a few spoken words.

- When: January 2024
- Type: Earlier work: mobile app concept, 1 week, solo
- Case study: https://rayasurya.com/earlier-work/sereni/

**What Raya designed.** Voice entries started from a reminder and recorded in the Dynamic Island, an emoji for each day, optional entry guides, progress insights, search by emoji or date, export to PDF and a dark mode. Research was a short survey and two personas.
